methods.name: Apply
methods.description:
Create or update a runner.

 @internal
 Primary registration path for CLI/Desktop runners. The handler determines
 whether to create or update based on whether the resource already exists
 (resolved by org + slug). Authorization is handled in the handler.

methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create a new runner.

 @internal
 Authorization: Caller must have can_create_runner permission in the
 organization. The server generates the task queue name (runner:{id})
 and sets the initial phase to PENDING.

methods.name: Update
methods.description:
Update an existing runner.

 @internal
 Used for updating spec fields (e.g., description). Status fields are
 updated via the connect stream heartbeat, not via this RPC.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete a runner.

 @internal
 For persistent runners: removes the resource and its task queue.
 For system-managed runners: called by the execution workflow during
 cleanup after the execution completes.

methods.name: SendCommand
methods.description:
Send a command to a connected runner and return the response synchronously.

 This is the API entry point for UI-triggered runner commands. The server
 looks up the runner's active bidi stream, pushes the command, and blocks
 until the runner responds or the timeout (10s) expires.

 Requires an active connect stream — returns UNAVAILABLE if the runner
 is not connected. Returns FAILED_PRECONDITION if the runner's phase
 prevents command delivery (STOPPED, PENDING, FAILED).

methods.name: Stop
methods.description:
Stop a running runner gracefully.

 If the runner is connected: sends a StopRunnerRequest via the bidi
 stream, waits for acknowledgment, then returns the updated Runner.
 The runner will send a STOPPED heartbeat and close its stream after
 acknowledging — the phase transition completes asynchronously.

 If the runner is not connected (offline, already stopped): directly
 transitions the runner to STOPPED and returns the updated resource.

 Idempotent: stopping an already-STOPPED or FAILED runner returns the
 resource as-is without error.

methods.name: Connect
methods.description:
Establish a bidirectional command stream between the runner and the server.

 This is the runner's primary ongoing communication channel. The runner
 pushes heartbeats (liveness + state); the server pushes commands
 (e.g., ListDirectory for workspace browsing). Both directions use the
 same open connection.

 Stream lifecycle:
   1. Runner calls apply to register/reactivate, then opens this stream.
   2. First message MUST be a RunnerHeartbeat (authenticates via runner_id).
   3. Runner sends heartbeats every 30s.
   4. Server pushes RunnerCommandRequest when the UI triggers an operation.
   5. Runner handles commands locally and sends RunnerCommandResponse.
   6. On graceful shutdown: runner sends phase=STOPPED heartbeat, closes stream.
   7. On disconnect: server starts heartbeat timeout (90s) -> STOPPED.

 @internal
 Authorization is handled via the first heartbeat message: the server
 looks up the runner_id and verifies ownership. Skipped at the interceptor
 level because the stream input is not a resource type.

methods.name: CreateLaunchToken
methods.description:
Create a one-time launch token for the browser-to-CLI runner handshake.

 Called by the web console when the user clicks "Launch Local Runner."
 The server mints a Stigmer JWT for the caller, wraps it in an opaque
 token stored in Redis (60s TTL, single-use), and returns the token for
 the browser to embed in a stigmer:// URL.

 The caller must have can_create_runner permission in the organization —
 if you can create a runner, you can create a launch token.

methods.name: ExchangeLaunchToken
methods.description:
Exchange a one-time launch token for long-lived runner credentials.

 Called by the CLI (or Desktop app) after receiving a stigmer:// URL from
 the OS. The token is consumed atomically — a second exchange attempt
 returns NOT_FOUND.

 @internal
 This RPC is public — no Bearer token is required. The one-time launch
 token IS the proof of authorization: it was created by an authenticated
 user with can_create_runner permission, and can only be used once.

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get a single runner by ID.

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description:
Get a runner by its organization-scoped reference (org/slug).

 Used by the CLI to resolve a runner by name:
   stigmer run agent my-agent --runner my-macbook
 resolves "my-macbook" to the full Runner resource.

 @internal
 Custom authorization in handler — checks both direct resource access
 and organization-level visibility permissions.

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List runners within an organization.

 Supports label-based filtering for common use cases:
 - Session composer: exclude system-managed runners, show only READY
 - Admin view: show all runners including system-managed
 - Debugging: filter by specific labels

 @internal
 Authorization is handled in-handler via FGA-filtered queries (cloud)
 or unrestricted store queries (OSS).

methodTypes.name: RunnerSendCommandInput
methodTypes.description:
RunnerSendCommandInput is the request for the sendCommand unary RPC.

 Allows API callers (web UI, CLI) to send a typed command to a connected
 runner and receive the response synchronously. The server wraps the command
 in a RunnerCommandRequest with a generated request_id, pushes it to the
 runner's bidi stream, and returns the runner's response.

 The command oneof mirrors RunnerCommandRequest.command — callers specify
 the command directly without dealing with stream protocol details like
 request_id.

fields.name: RunnerId
fields.description: ID of the runner to send the command to.

methodTypes.name: RunnerCommandResponse
methodTypes.description:
RunnerCommandResponse is the runner's reply to a RunnerCommandRequest.

 Sent on the connect stream after the runner handles a command locally.
 The request_id correlates this response to the original request.

fields.name: RequestId
fields.description: Echoed from RunnerCommandRequest.request_id.

methodTypes.name: RunnerStopInput
methodTypes.description:
RunnerStopInput is the request for the stop RPC.

 Separate from StopRunnerRequest because the RPC input carries the
 runner_id (identifying which runner to stop), while the stream command
 does not (the stream is already bound to a specific runner).

fields.name: RunnerId
fields.description: ID of the runner to stop.

fields.name: Reason
fields.description:
Optional reason for the stop. Logged on the runner and in audit.
 Example: "user requested via web console"

methodTypes.name: RunnerStreamClientMessage
methodTypes.description:
RunnerStreamClientMessage is the envelope for all runner-to-server messages
 on the connect bidi stream.

 The runner sends two types of messages:
 - Heartbeats: periodic liveness reports (every 30s)
 - Command responses: replies to server-initiated commands

methodTypes.name: RunnerStreamServerMessage
methodTypes.description:
RunnerStreamServerMessage is the envelope for all server-to-runner messages
 on the connect bidi stream.

 The server sends command requests when the UI or API triggers an operation
 that requires runner-side execution (e.g., browsing the runner's filesystem).

methodTypes.name: CreateLaunchTokenRequest
methodTypes.description:
CreateLaunchTokenRequest initiates a browser-to-CLI credential handshake.

 Called by the web console when the user clicks "Launch Local Runner." The
 server generates a one-time, short-lived opaque token that the browser
 passes to the local CLI via the stigmer:// URL scheme. The CLI then
 exchanges the token for long-lived credentials via exchangeLaunchToken.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization slug. The minted credentials will be scoped to this org.

methodTypes.name: CreateLaunchTokenResponse
methodTypes.description:
CreateLaunchTokenResponse contains the opaque launch token for the browser
 to embed in the stigmer:// URL.

fields.name: Token
fields.description:
Opaque, single-use token. Embed in the URL as:
 stigmer://launch-runner?token={token}&endpoint={grpc_endpoint}

fields.name: ExpiresAt
fields.description:
Absolute expiry time. The token becomes invalid after this timestamp
 (typically 60 seconds from creation).

methodTypes.name: ExchangeLaunchTokenRequest
methodTypes.description:
ExchangeLaunchTokenRequest is the CLI's side of the handshake.

 The CLI extracts the token from the stigmer:// URL and calls this RPC
 to obtain long-lived credentials. This RPC is public (unauthenticated) —
 the one-time token IS the proof of authorization.

fields.name: Token
fields.description: The opaque token received from the stigmer:// URL.

methodTypes.name: ExchangeLaunchTokenResponse
methodTypes.description:
ExchangeLaunchTokenResponse provides the CLI with everything it needs to
 operate as an authenticated runner: a Stigmer-signed JWT and the org scope.

 The response shape mirrors MintUserTokenResponse for consistency in how
 Stigmer returns credentials.

fields.name: AccessToken
fields.description:
Stigmer-signed JWT for authenticating subsequent runner operations
 (apply, connect, heartbeat). Use as Bearer token.

fields.name: TokenType
fields.description: Token type. Always "Bearer".

fields.name: ExpiresIn
fields.description: Token lifetime in seconds from the time of issuance.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization slug the credentials are scoped to. The CLI uses this
 when creating the runner resource via apply.

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource by org and slug.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Environment, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical format: "org/slug" (e.g., "stigmer/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource.

 When non-empty: must be a valid org slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 1-63 characters). Example: "stigmer", "acme-corp".

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 Use explicit org for cross-org references (e.g., marketplace resources).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, MCP_SERVER).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 1-63 characters.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
Version of the resource (optional, only applicable to versioned resources like Skills).
 Supports three formats:
 1. Empty/unset → Resolves to "latest" (most recent version)
 2. Tag name → Resolves to version with this tag (e.g., "stable", "v1.0")
 3. Exact hash → Immutable reference to specific version (e.g., "abc123...")

 Default behavior: Empty means "latest" (current version).
 This field is ignored for non-versioned resources.

 Examples:
 - version: ""           → Use latest version
 - version: "latest"     → Use latest version (explicit)
 - version: "stable"     → Use version tagged as "stable"
 - version: "v1.0"       → Use version tagged as "v1.0"
 - version: "abc123..."  → Use exact version with this hash (immutable)

methodTypes.name: ListRunnersRequest
methodTypes.description: ListRunnersRequest is the input for listing runners within an organization.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization slug to scope the listing.

fields.name: Labels
PageInfo
fields.description: Pagination options.

methodTypes.name: RunnerList
methodTypes.description: RunnerList is the response for listing runners.

fields.name: TotalCount
fields.description: Total number of runners matching the query.

fields.name: Items
fields.description: Runners in the current page.

enumTypes.name: RunnerPhase
enumTypes.description:
RunnerPhase tracks the operational state of a runner process.

 Phase transitions are driven by two sources:
 - The runner process itself (via connect stream heartbeat): PENDING -> STARTING -> READY, READY <-> BUSY
 - The server (via heartbeat timeout or explicit stop): any -> STOPPED, any -> FAILED

 Transition diagram:
   PENDING  -> STARTING (runner process launched, bootstrapping runtime)
   STARTING -> READY    (bootstrap complete, agent process started)
   PENDING  -> READY    (legacy: first heartbeat without STARTING phase)
   READY    -> BUSY     (runner reports max capacity reached)
   BUSY     -> READY    (runner reports capacity freed)
   READY    -> STOPPED  (heartbeat timeout or explicit stop)
   BUSY     -> STOPPED  (heartbeat timeout or explicit stop)
   STARTING -> STOPPED  (bootstrap failed or process killed)
   STOPPED  -> STARTING (runner restarts and begins bootstrapping)
   STOPPED  -> READY    (legacy: runner restarts without STARTING phase)
   any      -> FAILED   (unrecoverable error reported by runner or server)

values.name: RUNNER_PHASE_PENDING
values.description:
Resource created but no heartbeat received yet.
 This is the initial phase after create/apply, before the runner
 process has started polling its task queue and heartbeating.

values.name: RUNNER_PHASE_READY
values.description: Runner is heartbeating and accepting new executions.

values.name: RUNNER_PHASE_BUSY
values.description:
Runner is heartbeating but at maximum concurrent execution capacity.
 New executions should not be dispatched to this runner.

values.name: RUNNER_PHASE_STOPPED
values.description:
Runner has stopped heartbeating (timeout) or was explicitly stopped.
 The resource is retained for identity persistence — a runner that
 restarts and resumes heartbeating transitions back to READY.

values.name: RUNNER_PHASE_FAILED
values.description:
Unrecoverable error. Runner or server reported a fatal condition.
 Requires investigation; does not auto-recover on heartbeat.

values.name: RUNNER_PHASE_STARTING
values.description:
Runner process has been launched and is bootstrapping its runtime
 (downloading dependencies, extracting source, creating venv).
 The runner is heartbeating but not yet ready to accept executions.
 Transitions to READY once bootstrap completes and the agent process
 starts polling its task queue.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines whether
 users outside that organization can access the resource.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only members of the owning organization can access.
 This is the default for most resources.
 Named visibility_private to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Anyone can access (read) this resource.
 Used for marketplace-published resources (e.g., "stigmer/web-search").
 Write access still requires org membership.
 Named visibility_public to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

resourceDescription:
Runner represents a process that executes work on the Stigmer platform.

 Runners are the computational backbone of the platform. Every execution
 runs on a runner — whether auto-created by the platform for a cloud
 execution or started by a user on their own machine via CLI or desktop app.

 Runner follows the Kubernetes Node pattern:
 - **Thin spec**: the user declares intent (a name, a description). That's it.
 - **Rich status**: the runner process self-reports everything via the
   connect stream — phase, capacity, machine info, task queue.
 - **Identity persists across restarts**: a runner that stops and restarts
   reconnects to the same resource. The CLI stores the runner ID locally and
   calls apply to reactivate the same identity, same queue.

 Two creation patterns:
 - **User-created (persistent)**: user runs `stigmer runner start`, runner
   appears in the session composer, user selects it for their sessions.
 - **System-managed (ephemeral)**: platform auto-creates a runner for a cloud
   execution, labels it stigmer.ai/system-managed: "true", tears it down when
   the execution completes. Hidden from the session composer.

 Sessions bind to a runner via SessionSpec.runner_id. Executions record
 which runner handled them via AgentExecutionStatus.runner_id.

statusType.name: RunnerStatus
statusType.description:
RunnerStatus contains all operational state for a runner.

 Every field here is either system-managed (phase, task_queue) or
 runner-reported via heartbeat (last_heartbeat_at, current_executions,
 connection_info). None of it is user-declared — that separation is the
 spec/status invariant.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, created_by, etc.)

fields.name: Phase
fields.description: Current operational phase of the runner process.

fields.name: TaskQueue
fields.description:
Temporal task queue this runner polls for work.
 Format: "runner:{runner-id}"
 Set by the server when the runner resource is created; immutable after.
 The execution workflow reads this field to route activities to the runner.

fields.name: LastHeartbeatAt
fields.description:
Timestamp of the last successful heartbeat from the runner process.
 Used by the server to detect stale runners: if now - last_heartbeat_at
 exceeds the heartbeat timeout (default 90s), the phase transitions to
 STOPPED.

fields.name: StartedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when this runner first transitioned to READY.

fields.name: StoppedAt
fields.description:
Timestamp when this runner last transitioned to STOPPED or FAILED.
 Empty while the runner is active (PENDING, READY, or BUSY).

fields.name: CurrentExecutions
fields.description:
Number of executions currently in progress on this runner.
 Reported by the runner on each heartbeat. Used by the dispatch logic
 to determine runner availability and load.

fields.name: ConnectionInfo
fields.description:
Self-reported information about the machine running this runner.
 Populated by the runner process on each heartbeat.

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the actor.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.description: Actor who created this resource.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: RunnerConnectionInfo
statusNestedTypes.description:
RunnerConnectionInfo contains self-reported details about the runner's
 host environment. Populated by the runner process on each heartbeat
 message sent over the connect stream.

 This information is used for:
 - UI display: "Alice's MacBook Pro (darwin/arm64)"
 - Debugging: matching runner behavior to specific OS/arch combinations
 - Version tracking: ensuring runners stay up-to-date

fields.name: Hostname
fields.description:
Hostname or user-friendly machine name.
 Example: "Alice's MacBook Pro", "ci-runner-3.internal"

fields.name: Os
fields.description:
Operating system reported by the runner process.
 Example: "darwin", "linux", "windows"

fields.name: Arch
fields.description:
CPU architecture reported by the runner process.
 Example: "arm64", "amd64"

fields.name: RunnerVersion
fields.description:
Version of the runner software.
 Example: "0.4.2"

fields.name: MachineId
fields.description:
Stable machine identifier, generated once per Stigmer CLI installation
 and persisted at ~/.stigmer/machine.json. Used for runner deduplication
 across hostname changes. Format: "mach_" + 32 hex chars.
 Example: "mach_a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6"
